title: Fellow – Business-Society Relations
jobDescription:
1. POSITION VACANT: Fellow
- Business-Society Relations, Centre for Social and Economic Progress, Chanakyapuri, New Delhi
2. ORGANIZATION BACKGROUND: The Centre for Social and Economic Progress (CSEP) conducts in-depth, policy-relevant research and provides evidence-based recommendations to the challenges facing India and the world. It draws on the expertise of its researchers, extensive interactions with policymakers as well as convening power to enhance the impact of research. CSEP researchers work across domains including, but not limited to, Growth, Finance, Health and Human Development; Energy, Natural Resources and Sustainability; and Foreign Policy and Security. All CSEP research and policy recommendations are freely available to the public. CSEP is an independent, non-partisan research organisation based in New Delhi. It is registered as a company limited by shares and not for profit, under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013 (earlier Section 25 of the Companies Act, 1956). CSEP is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All persons regardless of race, colour, creed, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital status, disability, religious or political affiliation, age or sexual orientation shall have equal access to positions, limited only by their ability to do the job. The newly launched Programme on Business-Society Relations at CSEP, New Delhi, will investigate business-society relations and how various stakeholders perceive the responsibilities of Indian businesses towards society. Within this broad theme, the programme will research how Indian corporates are responding to emerging demands. The objective of the research will be to produce evidence-based, policy-relevant research at the intersection of business strategy, corporate governance, and public accountability of corporates. The research outputs will be disseminated through publications/ workshops and in an annual flagship event that will include a lecture by a globally recognised thought leader followed by a symposium on the theme.
3. JOB DESCRIPTION/

RESPONSIBILITIES:
Role Overview The research programme is directed by a Senior Fellow. The Fellow will work with the Senior Fellow and anchor the intellectual agenda of the programme. Operating with a high degree of independence, the incumbent will contribute to programme design, lead and partner with research streams, co-author studies, manage the work of research analyst(s) and produce agreed research outputs. The Fellow will also be required to represent CSEP in scholarly and policy forums. The role demands research, scholarly and policy engagement, interacting with national and global thought leaders, and contributing to India's corporate governance discourse. Advantages of Being Associated With CSEP (1) Opportunity to engage with policymakers, senior government officials, industry leaders and distinguished academics from leading global institutions. (2) Opportunity to grow and work at the forefront of collaboration with a diverse network of global partners, including multilateral organisations, research institutions, and leading industry stakeholders. Key Responsibilities The Fellow will be expected to: (1) Work on and be responsible for cutting-edge research streams, including conceptualisation, design, and delivery of findings on topics such as business-society relations, corporate legitimacy, stakeholder governance, and CSR policy in India. (2) Co-develop research designs combining theoretical analysis, case studies, expert interviews, stakeholder surveys, and analysis of regulatory disclosures. Help develop survey instruments and interview protocols. (3) Conduct literature reviews and synthesise international and Indian scholarship. (4) Undertake stakeholder interviews with corporate leaders, investors, regulators, civil society organisations and policymakers to ground research in practical realities and ensure policy uptake. (5) Produce high-quality research outputs including working papers, journal articles, policy briefs, and edited chapters, and take them through peer review and publication processes. (6) Present findings at conferences, roundtables and stakeholder consultations. (7) Participate in national and international conferences, roundtables, and executive forums, and contribute to public discourse through media and opinion articles. (8) Supervise, mentor, and provide intellectual guidance to junior researchers and other project staff. (9) Help plan and deliver the annual flagship event including the Annual Lecture and Symposium and other preparatory events leading up to the annual event. (10) Contribute to proposal writing for external funding and assist in programme planning, monitoring, and evaluation.
5. QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE AND COMPETENCIES: Essential Qualifications and Experience (1) Ph D in Management, Economics, Sociology, or a closely related discipline. (2) Formal training or advanced coursework in research methods (both qualitative and quantitative). Required Experience Essential (1) Minimum 5-7 years and maximum 15 years of high-quality research experience, with a demonstrable track record on business-related themes, preferably in the field of industrial organisation, corporate governance, business-society relations, etc. (2) A good publication record, including journal articles, book chapters, or equivalent scholarly outputs. (3) Demonstrated experience in mixed-methods research design, including stakeholder surveys, interviews, document analysis, and case study methodology. Preferred (1) Experience working at or closely with a policy research institution, think tank, regulator, or multilateral organisation. (2) Familiarity with India's corporate regulatory architecture, including the Companies Act 2013, SEBI's Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements (LODR) and Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) regulations, and allied frameworks. (3) Experience supervising junior researchers or managing research projects. (4) Experience engaging with senior corporate, government, or civil society stakeholders in a research or advisory capacity. Key Competencies and Skills Essential (1) Ability to design and execute independent research from conceptualisation through publication, with minimal supervision. (2) Strong theoretical foundation in at least one of the following fields: industrial organisation, corporate governance, business-society relations. (3) Excellent research writing and communication skills
- ability to produce both rigorous scholarly papers and accessible policy briefs for non-specialist audiences. (4) Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to represent CSEP credibly before senior stakeholders. (5) Ability to mentor and develop junior team members. Preferred (1) Working familiarity with quantitative analysis tools (STATA, R, or similar) and tools for qualitative data analysis. (2) Familiarity with globally recognised ESG rating methodologies and impact assessment frameworks such as GRI, TCFD, etc.
6. COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS: CSEP offers a competitive compensation package, commensurate with qualifications and experience, along with a comprehensive benefits package.

title: Head – Affiliated Organisations Cell
jobDescription:
1. POSITION VACANT: Head
- Affiliated Organisations Cell , Large Philanthropic Organisation, Mumbai
2. ORGANISATIONAL BACKGROUND: Our client is a respected philanthropic organisation with a vision of advancing humanitarian values and nation-building. The organisation drives social and economic development across India by focusing on health, education, livelihoods, water and sanitation, social inclusion, environment, and disaster response. Our client's mission is to empower underserved communities through innovative programmes and strategic collaborations with governments, civil society, and global partners, creating sustainable impact aligned with national priorities and the UN Sustainable Development Goals.
3. JOB DESCRIPTION/

RESPONSIBILITIES:
Reporting to the Senior Advisor , the Head
- Affiliated Organisations Cell (AOC) will establish and lead a centralised platform to support and strengthen the strategic direction, governance, administration, compliance, finance and operational effectiveness of multiple smaller trusts and affiliated entities within the organisation. The role will drive organisational transformation, operational excellence, resource optimisation, statutory compliance, and stakeholder management, while ensuring alignment with the values, governance standards, and strategic priorities of the parent organisation. The incumbent will act as the principal strategic and institutional leader for the Affiliated Organisations Cell , working closely with internal and external stakeholders to improve efficiency, enhance institutional effectiveness, and enable the long-term sustainability of the affiliated entities. The incumbent will develop Board-ready business cases and build Board alignment for transformation initiatives. Key

RESPONSIBILITIES:
(1) Establish and operationalise the Affiliated Organisations Cell as a centralised strategy, transformation, governance and administrative platform for multiple trusts and affiliated entities; (2) Drive consolidation and standardisation of core functions including administration, finance, taxation, compliance, HR, travel, and shared services, including modernisation of systems and processes and, where appropriate, leveraging capabilities available within the parent organisation; (3) Develop and implement trust-specific transformation plans and Board-ready business cases to ensure efficient resource utilisation across all Affiliated Organisations Cell initiatives; (4) Lead the setup, expansion, and operations of educational institutions falling within the ambit of the Affiliated Organisations Cell; (5) Build and manage strategic partnerships and lead stakeholder engagement by building trusted relationships with senior internal leadership, cross-functional teams, government authorities, auditors and regulatory agencies to support effective governance and organisational objectives; (6) Engage with municipal authorities to align initiatives with civic requirements and expectations; (7) Review trust-owned properties and other assets and recommend their optimal utilisation, including for education, healthcare and other public-purpose initiatives; (8) Strengthen governance by ensuring appropriate representation of the parent organisation on the boards of affiliated trusts and entities; (9) Drive strategic ownership arrangements, including securing majority or controlling interests in affiliated entities, where appropriate; (10) Oversee capital allocation to ensure prudent investment and funding for high-impact initiatives; (11) Identify and execute mergers and consolidation opportunities in compliance with legal and regulatory frameworks.
4. QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE AND COMPETENCIES: Qualifications Applicants must possess a postgraduate degree in Management, Finance, Public Policy, Law or another relevant discipline from a reputed institution. Experience (1) 15-20 years of experience in leadership roles spanning strategy, transformation, operations, administration, governance, finance or institutional management; (2) Demonstrated experience managing complex multi-stakeholder organisations, trusts, foundations, public institutions or large corporate shared-service environments; (3) Proven track record of developing robust business cases, influencing Boards and driving organisational transformation, consolidation initiatives and operational excellence. (4) Experience in the governance, establishment, expansion or operation of educational institutions, healthcare institutions and/or property and asset utilisation will be an advantage; (5) Exposure to mergers or consolidation, strategic ownership structures and capital allocation will be advantageous. Skills and Competencies (1) Strong understanding of governance frameworks, regulatory compliance and board processes; (2) Strategic leadership and institution building, including portfolio transformation; (3) Governance and Board management, including the ability to influence trustees and senior stakeholders; (4) Trusts, foundations and not-for-profit administration; (5) Financial and operational management, including business-case development and asset utilisation; (6) Regulatory and statutory compliance; (7) Stakeholder engagement and influencing skills. (8) Change management and organisational transformation; (9) Resource optimisation and shared services design; (10) Strong execution and problem-solving capability; (11) High degree of integrity, judgment and discretion. (12) Candidates with Gujarati language proficiency will have an added advantage. (13) Willingness to travel extensively.
5. COMPENSATION OFFERED: The compensation offered for the position is competitive and commensurate with experience and qualifications.
6. LOCATION & NATURE OF APPOINTMENT: (1) Location: Mumbai (2) Nature of Appointment: Full-time, on-roll position

title: Executive - Administration
jobDescription:
1. POSITION VACANT: Executive
- Administration, Large Philanthropic Organisation, Mumbai
2. ORGANISATIONAL BACKGROUND: Our client is a respected philanthropic organisation with a vision of advancing humanitarian values and nation-building. The organisation drives social and economic development across India by focusing on health, education, livelihoods, water and sanitation, social inclusion, environment, and disaster response. Our client's mission is to empower underserved communities through innovative programmes and strategic collaborations with governments, civil society, and global partners, creating sustainable impact aligned with national priorities and the UN Sustainable Development Goals.
3. JOB DESCRIPTION/

RESPONSIBILITIES:
Reporting to the Head
- Project Management Group , the Executive
- Administration shall support efficient administrative operations, with primary responsibility for administration budgeting, expenditure monitoring, MIS, vendor billing, AMC and contract records, and related financial documentation. This is an individual-contributor role within a small administration team and requires strong numerical ability, process rigour and close coordination with Administration, Procurement, Finance, vendors and service providers. The incumbent shall plan and monitor the annual administration budget, verify vendor invoices, exercise expenditure control, coordinate administration-related purchase requisitions with the Procurement team, monitor vendor and contract performance, and maintain accurate administration records. While the role is primarily desk-based and financially oriented, the incumbent shall share responsibility with the administration team for addressing urgent facilities and operational requirements across the Mumbai offices. Key

RESPONSIBILITIES:
(A) Annual Budget Planning & Financial Management: (1) Prepare the annual administration budget in consultation with relevant stakeholders; (2) Monitor actual expenditure against approved budgets and maintain accurate budget-utilisation trackers; (3) Conduct monthly budget-variance analysis and highlight material deviations in a timely manner; (4) Prepare financial and management reports relating to administration expenditure; and (5) Recommend practical cost-optimisation initiatives without compromising operational efficiency or service quality. (B) Billing & Invoice Management: (1) Review, verify and reconcile invoices received from vendors and service providers; (2) Ensure that invoices comply with contractual terms, approved purchase orders, statutory and tax-related documentation, and agreed commercial rates; (3) Resolve invoice discrepancies in coordination with vendors and relevant internal teams; and (4) Monitor recurring monthly invoices and payments and support timely processing. (C) Purchase Requisition & Procurement Coordination: (1) Consolidate administration-related requirements based on operational needs and approved budgets; (2) Raise complete and accurate Purchase Requisitions with the required technical and commercial details; (3) Liaise with the Procurement team and provide administrative and operational inputs for vendor quotations and evaluation, as required; and (4) Track pending purchase requests and follow up to support the timely delivery of goods and services. (D) Vendor Management: (1) Evaluate vendor and service-provider performance against agreed Service Level Agreements and operational requirements; (2) Support the Procurement team by providing administrative and operational inputs for vendor selection, due diligence and onboarding, as required; (3) Maintain an updated vendor database and complete supporting documentation; and (4) Build constructive working relationships with vendors while ensuring accountability, service quality and value for money. (E) Administrative & Facilities Operations: (1) Work as part of the administration team to support the day-to-day functioning of office facilities and address urgent operational requirements; (2) Coordinate the maintenance of non-IT office infrastructure, utilities and facilities equipment; (3) Supervise and monitor housekeeping, security, reception, pantry and other facility service providers; (4) Monitor inventory levels of office supplies and consumables and support timely replenishment; and (5) Ensure that preventive-maintenance schedules are maintained and followed. (F) Contract & AMC Management: (1) Maintain accurate records of vendor contracts and Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMCs); (2) Monitor contract and AMC expiry dates and initiate renewal processes sufficiently in advance; (3) Track vendor obligations, service deliverables and relevant compliance requirements; and (4) Maintain documentation required for internal review and audit compliance, coordinate periodic asset verification, and support responses to administration-related audit queries. (G) Key Stakeholders: (1) Relationship within the organisation: Theme Heads, Function Heads, Procurement, Finance and other internal teams; (2) Relationship outside the organisation: Vendors and service providers.
4. QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE AND COMPETENCIES: Qualifications CA Inter / Master of Commerce with 5 years of experience or Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Commerce, Finance or any related discipline with 6-10 years of experience in Administration, Facilities Management, or Corporate Services Experience (1) About 5-10 years of relevant experience in administration, administration finance, facilities management or corporate services, preferably in a structured corporate or institutional environment; (2) Strong working knowledge of budgeting, expense management, procurement coordination, vendor management, contract administration and audit compliance; (3) Hands-on experience in invoice verification and reconciliation, purchase requisition workflows, expenditure monitoring and financial reporting; (4) Experience in managing multiple vendors and service providers and coordinating with cross-functional stakeholders; and (5) Experience in maintaining contract, vendor and compliance documentation with a high degree of accuracy. Skills and Competencies (1) Strong budgeting, financial planning, analytical and reporting skills; (2) Sound understanding of expense management, cost control and financial discipline; (3) Knowledge of procurement processes, purchase requisitions and vendor-governance practices; (4) Strong vendor, stakeholder and relationship-management skills; (5) Excellent attention to detail, documentation accuracy and follow-through; (6) Strong problem-solving and practical decision-making abilities; (7) Good planning, organising and project-coordination skills; (8) Clear written and verbal communication and effective interpersonal skills; (9) Advanced working proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including the ability to consolidate, reconcile and analyse data across multiple worksheets and system-generated reports, along with proficiency in Word and Power Point; and (10) High integrity, accountability and the ability to work independently as well as collaboratively.
5. COMPENSATION OFFERED: The compensation offered for the position is competitive and commensurate with experience and salary history.
6. LOCATION & NATURE OF APPOINTMENT: (1) Location: Mumbai; (2) Nature of Appointment: Fixed-term employment for three years. (3) Preference will be given to candidates currently based in Mumbai and available to join at short notice.

title: Assistant Manager-Corporate Partnerships
jobDescription:
1. POSITION VACANT: Assistant Manager-Corporate Partnerships, SOS Children's Villages of India, Mumbai

jobDescription:

- Implementation, Room to Read India, Bangalore, Karnataka
2. ORGANISATION BACKGROUND : Room to Read India was established in 2003 and presently has programs in twelve states
- Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Delhi NCR, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Telangana, Uttarakhand, and Uttar Pradesh. Room to Read is a global organization transforming the lives of millions of children by focusing on literacy and gender equality in education. Since 2000, Room to Read has benefited more than 52 million children across 29 countries. For more information about, Room to Read India please visit: www.roomtoreadindia.org .
3. JOB DESCRIPTION/

RESPONSIBILITIES:
The Lead
- Implementation is responsible for Room to Read's operations in a geographic area, a state in this case. S/he is primarily responsible for ensuring government relations at state level, timely and effective implementation of programs at the field office, including implementation, spending, hiring, local procurement, inventory management, distribution and logistical support. The position is required to take initiative for project management, improving work approaches, partnerships, selection of projects sites, and ensuring adequate staff to work at the field level. The incumbent will work to strengthen coordination and collaboration within teams and across all CO (Country Office) program teams, maintaining and ensuring constructive communication, building team morale within individual teams and contributing to a positive working environment. S/he will report to the Principal Lead
- Implementation and will have dotted line reporting to various stakeholders from the Country Leadership Team. The entire state team will report to Lead- Implementation. Key Job

RESPONSIBILITIES:
A. System Strengthening and System Integration: (1) Working closely with State officials in ensuring government system strengthening and institutionalization of Rt R programs in the states; (2) Preparation of overall strategic plan, basis local context and Rt R Vision plan 2025 for the respective state and continuously reviewing the same; (3) Organizing various discussions/consultations with Government to work towards system strengthening and positioning Rt R as a thought leader in Literacy and Girls Education program; (4) Building body of evidence that can push appropriate policy/practice changes backed by robust evidence; (5) Support INCO Op's in proposal development and country growth plan as needed B. External Coordination, B randing, and Networking: (1) Attends to donor affairs including hosting donor and project site visits in collaboration with programs staff; (2) Develop and lead media advocacy plan for the state; (3) Assist Rt R communication team in promotion of Rt R programs through active media liasioning in state in accordance with the strategy, policies and guidelines of Rt R; (4) Scanning of education landscape in the state and positioning Rt R as a thought leader through strategic management; (5) Take lead in dissemination of program results, sharing program report to government and other agencies in suggestions with OPS team; (6) Meets regularly with local government representatives, NGO partners, school administrators and parent groups to represent Rt R; (7) Promotes and protects the reputation of Room to Read in external settings, ensuring that the organization's experience and expertise is well communicated and consistently presented, and that we are looked upon as a professional Education organization. C. Management and Coordination: (1) Ensures efficient and effective coordination across all elements of the Literacy Program and Girls' Education Program in his/her region; (2) Supervises and oversees the work of the field staff and is responsible for optimizing their productivity through effective management and leadership techniques (i.e., coaching/advising); (3) Ensures staff are consistently complying and adhering to policies, procedures and guidelines articulated in the CO handbooks and facilitates the dissemination of information to all staff members to promote transparency; (4) Supports staff through consultation with CO-level technical team to regularly assess staff capacity building needs; (5) Ensures the performance management process is well-planned and conducted in a timely manner for all field staff. This includes setting performance goals, conducting progress check-ins, providing feedback, conducting year-end appraisals, and making recommendations for staff development and career advancement; (6) Collaborates with Human Resources to handle recruitment and training of staff according to need; (7) Leads and facilitates field staff in bi-weekly or monthly meetings to review progress against plans, find solutions to problems, share lessons learned, exchange expertise across programs, and to motivate and encourage teamwork; (8) Ensures that field-staff are aware of and understand the programs' goals and objectives, working approaches and methodology, and have all necessary information related to annual plans, targets, and implementation calendars; (9) Conducts regular field visits to monitor and verify the programs' progress and impact, understand the challenges, and needs of stakeholders (e.g., Rt R staff, Social Mobilizers, Field Facilitators, communities, children, etc.), and suggest appropriate solutions; (10) Develop and implement plans for on-line material development in consultation with Country office as per the state specific context; (11) Perform other tasks as assigned by the Sr. Manager
- Operations and Country Management Team. D. Financial Management: (1) Supervises fund disbursement, reviews and approves the field monthly and quarterly financial expenses in accordance with financial and purchasing policy and procedures; (2) Timely submission of cash forecast, booking of monthly bills and variance tracker; (3) Monthly tracking of all expense vis-à-vis the budgets and flagging any deviations to concerned person; (4) Coordinates the timely completion of annual planning and budgeting; (5) Ensuring full utilisation of respective budgets as per the financial guidelines; (6) Co-ordinate and answer any audit queries for the state. E. Reporting and Documentation : (1) Develops high quality quarterly report for distributing to partners, if applicable; (2) Prepares high quality monthly and quarterly donor programmatic reports, coordinate with concerned Program, Finance and OP's department in INCO for finalizing and sharing the report on time; (3) Ensuring high level of data quality for all reporting purposes; (4) Preparation of appropriate case studies for submission to donors/communication team. F. Percentages of Work of State Head: Tasks for State Head Allocation of % on the tasks System Integration and strengthening 30% Management and Coordination 35% Financial Management 25% Monitoring, Donor Visit and Govt visits 2% Training & Development 8%
4. QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE AND COMPETENCIES:

QUALIFICATIONS:
(1) Master's degree in Education, Social Sciences, Social Work, Management, or a related discipline. Experience: (1) Minimum 12 years of relevant experience, including at least 5 years of management experience in related sector; (2) Experience in working closely with Government departments and education systems; (3) Prior experience in community engagement and mobilization, stakeholder management, and partnership development; (4) Proficiency in the local language will be preferred. Skills & Competencies : (1) Strong strategic planning and leadership capabilities; (2) Excellent program and project management skills; (3) Strong government liaisoning, stakeholder engagement, and partnership-building abilities; (4) Proven people management and team development skills; (5) Strong financial planning, budgeting, and resource management capabilities; (6) Excellent analytical, problem-solving, communication, and reporting skills; (7) Passion for improving education outcomes, literacy, and gender equality.
5. COMPENSATION OFFERED: Room to Read offers a competitive salary with excellent benefits. Benefits include thirteenth month bonus, health insurance and a retirement plan. The non-monetary compensation includes a unique opportunity to be part of an innovative, meaningful, and rapidly growing organization that is changing transforming the lives of millions of children in developing countries on literacy and gender equality in education.

jobDescription:
Title: Program Manager Location: New Delhi, India Organizational Overview Headquartered in New York, Smile Train is an international not-for-profit, with the mission of transforming the life of every child impacted by cleft lip and palate. The organization trains and supports doctors and medical professionals to provide free, life-changing, and comprehensive, cleft treatment, to afflicted children. Smile Train's sustainable model has helped improve the lives of 1.5 million children in 90+ countries, to date. The organization is committed to changing the world, one smile at a time. The organization has been operational in India for the past 22 years and successfully carried out more than 700,000 free cleft surgeries to date. For more details about Smile Train, please visit: https://www.smiletrainindia.org/ Make a Difference! As Smile Train's Program Manager , the Program Manager serves as the primary point of contact and representative for Smile Train's programs within the assigned region, reporting to the Area Director
- South Asia. The role is responsible for managing partner relationships and overseeing the implementation, quality, compliance, and continuous improvement of Smile Train's cleft treatment programs in alignment with country, regional, and global strategies. Working closely with partner hospitals, healthcare professionals, and internal teams, the Program Manager strengthens programme quality, builds institutional capacity, and expands access to safe, comprehensive cleft care across India. The role requires frequent travel to partner locations, including remote areas, and plays a key role in improving healthcare outcomes for children born with cleft lip and palate. Reports To The Area Director
- South Asia Key Responsibilities The Program Manager shall be responsible for the following: (A) Relationship Management (1) Serve as the primary relationship manager for partner hospitals and treatment teams within the assigned area. (2) Maintain regular communication with partners to support program implementation and ensure alignment with Smile Train policies and expectations. (3) Address partner inquiries, operational challenges, and patient-related concerns in a timely and solution-oriented manner. (4) Liaise with partners to gather required administrative documentation including credentialing information, reports, surveys, and program updates. (5) Ensure partners understand and comply with Smile Train's protocols, reporting requirements, and partnership agreements. (6) Support onboarding of new partners and practitioners in coordination with internal teams. (7) Escalate risks, compliance issues, or operational concerns to the Area Director when required. (B) Program Implementation (1) Oversee implementation of Smile Train programs within the assigned geographic area. (2) Conduct regular monitoring visits to partner hospitals to assess program performance, safety practices, compliance, and patient care standards. (3) Review program data including surgical outputs, compliance indicators, and documentation to monitor partner performance. (4) Work with partners to address program gaps and support implementation of operational improvements. (5) Facilitate the addition of treatment types and practitioner accreditation processes where appropriate. (6) Support implementation of partner training initiatives, workshops, and webinars to strengthen program quality and compliance. (7) Coordinate with internal teams, medical advisors, and subject matter experts to support partner program development. (C) Compliance (1) Monitor partner compliance with Smile Train policies including patient record submission, safety protocols, and reporting requirements. (2) Facilitate safety audits, quality reviews, and other compliance processes for partner hospitals. (3) Track and follow up on action items arising from audits, reviews, and monitoring visits. (4) Support management of sentinel events and ensure appropriate reporting and documentation. (5) Address patient complaints or feedback in coordination with partners and escalate issues when necessary. (6) Ensure partners adhere to branding, documentation, and partnership agreement requirements. (D) Financial Management (1) Monitor partner budget utilization within the assigned area to ensure appropriate use of program funds. (2) Review and process partner funding applications in accordance with Smile Train program guidelines. (3) Support financial audits and follow up on corrective actions where necessary. title: Technical Specialist (TB & Lung Diseases)
jobDescription:
1. POSITION VACANT: Technical Specialist (TB & Lung Diseases), The International Union Against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease, Telangana
2. ORGANISATIONAL BACKGROUND: The International Union Against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease ( The Union ), established in 1920, is a global membership, technical and scientific organisation working to end suffering caused by tuberculosis (TB) and lung disease. Its worldwide membership brings together government and non-government agencies, professional bodies, donors and funders, patient and survivor groups, clinicians, researchers, policymakers, frontline workers, programme implementers, advocates and civil society organisations. The Union generates, shares and applies knowledge to strengthen the prevention, diagnosis, treatment and care of TB and lung disease. Its work encompasses scientific and operational research, technical assistance, programme implementation, capacity strengthening and policy engagement, helping translate evidence into effective public-health policies and practices. Across its work, The Union seeks to ensure that vulnerable and marginalised populations are not left behind and is guided by a commitment to quality, transparency, accountability, respect and independence. The Union Office in India provides public-health expertise to governments, civil society, corporations and international agencies across South-East Asia, particularly in the areas of TB prevention and care and tobacco control. It also undertakes operational research, capacity-building programmes and grant-monitoring services, working closely with government health systems and other partners to strengthen programme implementation and improve public-health outcomes. For more information, please visit https://theunion.org/our-work/south-east-asia
3. JOB DESCRIPTION/

RESPONSIBILITIES:
Reporting to the Head of Programmes (TB & Lung Diseases), The Union India Office, the Technical Specialist will provide technical and programmatic support for the implementation of tuberculosis-related projects under The Union India Office. The position will support project planning, technical implementation, monitoring and evaluation, stakeholder coordination, reporting, and documentation of programme outcomes. The Technical Specialist will work closely with government counterparts, project teams, consultants, and technical partners to ensure high-quality implementation of project activities in accordance with national TB programme priorities, donor requirements, and The Union's technical standards. Key Job

RESPONSIBILITIES:
A. Technical Support and Programme Implementation (1) Provide technical assistance for the implementation of TB-related projects and activities across project states and sites; (2) Coordinate with State and District TB Cells, as relevant; (3) Support the development and execution of annual workplans, implementation plans, activity schedules, and project monitoring frameworks; (4) Ensure project activities are implemented in accordance with approved workplans, budgets, donor requirements, and national guidelines; (5) Support the adaptation and dissemination of technical guidance, tools, standard operating procedures, and training materials; (6) Assist in identifying implementation challenges and recommend practical solutions to improve programme performance; (7) Lead the development of clinical trial and operational research study protocols, implementation of research activities, and adherence to research ethics requirements; (8) Prepare project progress reports and other reports, as relevant. B. Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting (1) Manage routine monitoring of project activities, outputs, and performance indicators; (2) Support data collection and data analysis activities; (3) Analyse programme data and contribute to evidence-based decision-making and programme improvements; (4) Manage the preparation of monthly, quarterly, annual, and donor reports; (5) Ensure documentation of best practices, lessons learned, success stories, and programme achievements; (6) Lead data quality assessments, monitoring visits, and supportive supervision activities. C. Capacity Building and Technical Assistance (1) Support the planning and delivery of training programmes, workshops, and capacity-building initiatives for healthcare providers, programme staff, and stakeholders; (2) Provide technical support to state and district-level implementation teams; (3) Mentor project staff, consultants, volunteers, and implementing partners on technical and programmatic matters. D. Stakeholder Coordination (1) Maintain effective working relationships with national, state, and district TB programme stakeholders; (2) Participate in technical meetings, consultations, workshops, and review meetings, representing The Union as assigned. E. Other Responsibilities (1) Support proposal development, technical concept notes, and programme design activities, as required; (2) Undertake field visits to project locations for technical support, monitoring, and stakeholder engagement; (3) Perform any other duties assigned by the Head of Programmes.
4. QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE AND COMPETENCIES: Qualification: Applicants must possess a Medical Doctor (MBBS) qualification or a Master's degree in Public Health, Epidemiology, Health Management, Community Medicine, Biostatistics, Clinical Research, or another relevant discipline. Experience: (1) Minimum seven years of professional experience in tuberculosis, public health programmes, clinical research, or related health-sector initiatives; (2) Experience in clinical trials, implementation research, operational research, study coordination, research ethics, data management, and documentation is essential; (3) Demonstrated experience supporting the implementation of public health or TB programmes at national or sub-national level; (4) Strong understanding of India's National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP), including TB prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care; (5) Good understanding of research methods, epidemiology, biostatistics, study design, sampling approaches, and statistical analysis; (6) Experience in monitoring and evaluation, data analysis, programme reporting, and performance monitoring; (7) Experience coordinating with government agencies, development partners, ethics committees, research institutions, and implementing organisations. Skills and Competencies: (1) Excellent analytical, communication, presentation, and report-writing skills; (2) Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively in a multidisciplinary environment; (3) Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, data management tools, and statistical software will be an advantage; (4) Excellent written and spoken English; (5) Technical expertise in TB programming; (6) Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; (7) Effective stakeholder engagement and collaboration; (8) Results-oriented approach with attention to quality; (9) Ability to work independently and as part of a team; (10) Commitment to The Union's mission, vision, and values; (11) Willingness and ability to travel extensively within India.
5. COMPENSATION OFFERED: Gross compensation budgeted for the position is attractive. The offer made to the selected candidate shall be commensurate with qualifications, experience, and salary history.
6. DURATION OF CONTRACT: Until 31 December 2027, extendable based on funds availability and performance.
7. TRAVEL: As necessary

2. ORGANIZATION BACKGROUND: Pure Earth is a global leader in improving public health and development outcomes by reducing exposure to lead and other toxic pollutants. The organisation works closely with governments, public health institutions, researchers, and local organisations to identify sources of toxic exposure, generate actionable evidence, and embed sustainable solutions into public systems at national scale. Lead poisoning is one of the world's most significant yet solvable environmental health challenges, disproportionately affecting children and vulnerable communities. Pure Earth is internationally recognised for its leadership in preventing lead exposure and supporting durable government-led systems for long-term lead poisoning prevention. Pure Earth is currently in a phase of significant growth and expansion, supported by strategic partnerships with governments, philanthropies, and development institutions. This includes major multi-year support from Bloomberg Philanthropies and The Audacious Project to accelerate and scale lead poisoning prevention efforts in India and globally. Pure Earth 's work is inherently cross-sectoral, requiring engagement across public health, environment, pollution control, manufacturing, industry, consumer safety, and regulatory ecosystems. Its work contributes directly to reducing toxic exposure, particularly among children, improving long-term developmental and health outcomes, and enabling safer, healthier communities. Pure Earth India, registered as P.E. Lead India Pvt Ltd, is a wholly owned subsidiary of Pure Earth , providing technical and implementation support for all India-based operations. With a central office in New Delhi, Pure Earth India currently supports work across Bihar, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Jharkhand, Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh and with plans to expand to Assam and Rajasthan in India, and operations in Nepal. Please visit https://www.pureearth.org/india/ to learn more about Pure Earth India .
3. JOB DESCRIPTION /

RESPONSIBILITIES:
Pure Earth India is seeking a rigorous, analytically strong, and systems-oriented Monitoring, Learning & Evaluation (MLE) Manager to build and lead its monitoring, learning, and evaluation function in India. This is a foundational role. The selected candidate will design Pure Earth India's MLE architecture from the ground up, ensuring that evidence is at the centre of programme design, implementation, review, adaptation, and reporting. This is not a routine compliance-monitoring role. Pure Earth India is looking for someone who thinks deeply about what good looks like, can translate complex programme logic into measurable outcomes, and has the technical skills to build systems that generate real-time, decision-relevant data. The position offers an opportunity to contribute to high-impact environmental health interventions, generating actionable evidence on the pathways to reduce lead exposure. (A) Theory of Change & MLE Framework Design (1) Lead the design and refinement of Theories of Change (To Cs) for Pure Earth India's state-level programmes, in close collaboration with programme and technical teams; (2) Develop comprehensive monitoring and evaluation plans, including outcome indicators, data collection methodologies, baselines, targets, reporting rhythms, and learning questions; (3) Translate programme objectives, implementation strategies, and expected outcomes into practical, measurable, and field-usable MLE frameworks. (B) Data Collection, Measurement & Quality Assurance (1) Design quantitative and qualitative data collection tools including household surveys, source assessment tools, key informant interview guides, focus group discussion protocols, observational checklists, and field monitoring formats; (2) Oversee field-level data collection processes, ensuring data quality, consistency, completeness, and ethical handling of programme data; (3) Establish and maintain data management systems, quality assurance protocols, and documentation standards across programmes. 4. 5. IDEAL CANDIDATE PROFILE: The ideal candidate is a hands-on MLE professional who combines strong statistical and data capability with the ability to design and implement practical monitoring systems in real programme settings. The candidate should be able to conceptualise what meaningful programme progress and outcomes should look like, develop MLE frameworks and tools from scratch, work with programme and field teams to implement these systems, and generate timely analysis that helps leadership and programme teams make better decisions. The role is particularly suited to candidates who are comfortable operating in a growing organisation where systems are still being built, and who can bring structure, rigour, and clarity without overcomplicating field implementation. Candidates who have worked only on routine MIS, compliance reporting, or academic research, without substantial experience designing MLE frameworks, tools, analysis systems, or learning loops for implementation programmes, are unlikely to be suitable. Candidates available to join immediately or at short notice shall be preferred.
6. COMPENSATION OFFERED: Gross compensation budgeted for the position is in the range of Rs 20 to 30 lacs per annum. The offer made to the selected candidate shall be commensurate with experience, suitability, and salary history.
7. NUMBER OF VACANCIES: One

title: Director Programmes
jobDescription:
1. POSITION VACANT: Director Programmes, Water Aid India, New Delhi
2. ORGANISATIONAL BACKGROUND: Jal Seva Charitable Foundation ( JSCF ) is registered in India as a not-for-profit company under Chapter 8 of the Companies Act,
2013. JSCF is an associate member of the Water Aid federation and uses the brand name ‘ Water Aid ' in India . Water Aid India ( WAI ) seeks to improve the quality of life of 5,000,000 households with a special emphasis on the vulnerable by 2029 through the provision of climate-resilient and sustainable WASH services. This will be achieved through demonstration, institution strengthening, and the effective utilization of public resources. WAI works in rural and urban areas, striving to deepen its presence in the states where it operates and expand its efforts to small towns. Thanks to its amazing supporters, WAI has reached millions of people with three essentials: clean water, decent toilets, and good hygiene, helping communities unlock their potential, break free from the cycle of poverty, and transform lives for good. Operational in 10 states across the country, WAI 's programme focus for the next five years is on ensuring access to safe and assured drinking water for households, as well as safely managed sanitation at both the household and habitation levels. WAI aims to ensure that anganwadis, schools, and healthcare facilities are equipped with adequate and appropriate water, sanitation, and hygiene infrastructure. The organisation seeks to develop integrated water and sanitation solutions in small towns. Across all these efforts, ensuring the climate resilience of infrastructure and systems remains a critical priority. WAI plans to achieve this through demonstration and by providing technical and knowledge support to governments at all levels, facilitating large-scale adoption. Implementation is carried out primarily through WAI 's own field teams. For more information about WAI , please visit: https://www.wateraid.org/in/
3. JOB DESCRIPTION/

RESPONSIBILITIES:
Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer , the Director Programmes (DP) will provide strategic and operational leadership for all programme-related initiatives of WAI , ensuring impactful delivery, collaboration with stakeholders, and alignment with the organisation's mission and values. As a key member of the Senior Management Team, the DP will drive programme implementation, ensure quality assurance, foster partnerships, and represent the organisation across various platforms. Key Job

RESPONSIBILITIES:
A. Leading Programme Implementation (1) Lead programme implementation across all the locations that WAI works in. Adopt a consensual and collaborative approach for programme delivery that empowers those primarily responsible for facilitating change and impact; (2) Ensure that programmes keep the community at their centre while maintaining the highest standards, cost-effectiveness and appropriateness; (3) Facilitate the identification and creation of standardised processes and systems that can facilitate delivery of impact to meet the organisation's strategic ambition; (4) Planning, creation of budgets, continuous review of performance against plans, and review of expenditures against budgets will be an integral part of programme implementation. (5) Identify the key gaps and opportunities in the external public policy and service delivery environments where WAI 's programmatic interventions can bring about high impact and progressive change. B. Quality Assurance (1) Ensure delivery on time, cost-effectively and with assurance of the requisite quality. Monitor the qualitative and quantitative outcomes and impact of the programme in collaboration with the Programme Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning team, to ensure successful implementation in line with the plan. (2) Lead the integration of strategic themes, cross-cutting issues, and implementation of global programme frameworks, policies, and standards throughout the organisation, and ensure that all programmes (at state or regional levels) are aligned with these. C. Working with Governments Enable WAI's pathway to scale by strengthening the provision of technical support to government at the Union, State and District levels. This will include supporting capacity building on technical aspects, as well as facilitating the design and implementation of water, sanitation and hygiene solutions that are appropriate for disadvantaged communities and responsive to the environment. The DP will ensure effective collaboration between the Programme team and the Policy and Technical Support team to advance this agenda. D. WAI as a Learning Organisation Foster and promote a culture of innovation, experimentation, reflection, and learning, ensuring that WAI continues to remain a frontrunner in the water, sanitation and hygiene space. The DP will help institutionalise practices that enable teams to draw upon evidence, field experience, and programme learnings to continuously strengthen programme quality and impact. E. Nurturing Leadership Coach, guide, and mentor staff under direct supervision so that they are effective as leaders and senior managers, and the culture of nurturing percolates to all levels in the team. Encourage and promote empowering and collaborative leadership, effective management, and a culture of openness and accountability in line with WAI 's values. F. Member of the Senior Management Team (SMT) Be an active member of the SMT and contribute to strategic direction, organisational decision-making, and other management-related issues. G. Foster Partnerships Work closely with the Resource Mobilisation team to help establish and maintain partnerships with a diverse set of individuals and institutions to help achieve the organisation's strategic ambition. H. Sectoral Representation Represent WAI in national civil society organisation, donor, and government forums related to water, sanitation and hygiene so as to influence thinking of other stakeholders on effective delivery and build WAI 's reputation as a sector leader.
4. QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE AND COMPETENCIES: Qualification: Applicants must have a post-graduate degree in public policy, public health, law, urban planning, rural development, management, environmental engineering/management or social sciences. Experience: (1) Minimum 15 years of overall experience, with 5-10 years in senior management roles and at least five years in a community-level implementation role. (2) An understanding of the water, sanitation and hygiene sector in India, key sector stakeholders and networks shall be preferred. Skills and Competencies: (1) Proven experience of leading programmes/operations that lead to impact at scale and transformational change; (2) Demonstrated ability to build collaborative partnerships and alliances for programme delivery; (3) Demonstrated expertise of leading, managing, and motivating others, and building high performing teams; (4) Excellent interpersonal and written communication skills; (5) Experience of raising and managing income.
5. COMPENSATION OFFERED: Gross compensation budgeted for the position is attractive. The offer made to the selected candidate shall be commensurate with qualifications, experience, and salary history.

- Programs, The Right to Sight (VISION 2020 INDIA), New Delhi
2. ORGANIZATION BACKGROUND: The Right to Sight India (VISION 2020 INDIA) was established in 2004 as a national platform dedicated to eliminating avoidable blindness across India. Operating as a not-for-profit organization, it serves as a pivotal contributor to the global initiative led by the World Health Organization ( WHO ) and the International Agency for the Prevention of Blindness ( IAPB ) to reduce preventable visual impairments. This initiative represents a collaborative partnership among INGOs, NGOs, and Dr. RP Centre, AIIMS, working collectively to enhance eye care programs, exchange knowledge, and develop innovative solutions to deliver high-quality, comprehensive, and equitable eye care. 3. JOB DESCRIPTION/

Key Job

title: Graphic Designer
jobDescription:

2. ORGANIZATION BACKGROUND: The Centre for Social and Economic Progress (CSEP) conducts in-depth, policy-relevant research and provides evidence-based recommendations to the challenges facing India and the world. It draws on the expertise of its researchers, extensive interactions with policymakers as well as convening power to enhance the impact of research. CSEP researchers work across domains including, but not limited to, Growth, Finance, Health and Human Development; Energy, Natural Resources and Sustainability; and Foreign Policy and Security. All CSEP research and policy recommendations are freely available to the public. CSEP is an independent, non-partisan research organisation based in New Delhi. It is registered as a company limited by shares and not for profit, under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013 (earlier Section 25 of the Companies Act, 1956). Working at CSEP provides a unique opportunity to collaborate with leading scholars and policy experts, and to contribute to high-quality outputs that inform public debate and policymaking at the national and global level. The institution fosters a collaborative, intellectually stimulating work environment and offers staff members the chance to build expertise across diverse policy domains. For more information about CSEP, please visit https://csep.org/
3. JOB DESCRIPTION/

RESPONSIBILITIES:
CSEP is looking for a Graphic Designer to join the Communications team and work closely with researchers across verticals. The position requires strong design fundamentals, editorial judgement, and the ability to translate complex research into clear, compelling, and visually engaging outputs . The ideal candidate should be organised, detail-oriented, eager to learn, and able to think on their feet, adapting design approaches to different kinds of research and communication needs while maintaining high standards of clarity, consistency, and aesthetics. S/he will be responsible for the layout and design of CSEP 's research outputs, including research papers, annual reports, briefs, and other publications. The chosen candidate will also create print and digital communication assets for events, conferences, and social media. The role requires a strong foundation in publication design and the ability to balance creativity with precision, while ensuring alignment and consistency with CSEP 's identity and quality standards. Key

RESPONSIBILITIES:
The Graphic Designer will be expected to: (1) Implement the layout and typesetting of research papers, reports, and other publications, ensuring accuracy, readability, and visual coherence; (2) Design covers and visuals for research outputs across verticals, translating content into thoughtful design solutions, in collaboration with the Communications team and researchers; (3) Interpret research content and make editorial design decisions relating to structure, hierarchy, use of charts/graphics, etc.; (4) Create communication collaterals including event materials, social media creatives, presentations, and conference assets (e.g., backdrops, standees, brochures); (5) Conduct final quality checks on all outputs (alignment, typography, consistency, print readiness, etc.); (6) Prepare files for digital and print production; (7) Manage multiple projects and adhere to stipulated timelines.
4. QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE AND COMPETENCIES: Qualifications and Experience: (1) Bachelor's degree or Diploma in Graphic Design, Visual Communication, Fine Arts, Multimedia, or a related discipline. Candidates with equivalent professional experience and a strong portfolio are also encouraged to apply; (2) Two to three years of work experience, with a strong portfolio in print and digital publication; (3) Proficiency in Adobe In Design (critical), Illustrator, Photoshop, and Acrobat; (4) Strong understanding of typography, layout systems, and information hierarchy; (5) Experience with tools like Canva or Power Point for template design; (6) Prior experience in think tanks, research organisations, publishing, or media is preferred. Skills and Competencies: (1) Ability to work confidently with text and data-heavy documents; (2) Strong editorial judgement- can assess what a document needs structurally and visually; (3) Ability to work efficiently (collaboratively and independently) under deadlines, with high attention to detail; (4) Confidence in taking initiative and proposing design improvements proactively; (5) Familiarity with data visualisation and chart styling; (6) Basic knowledge of video editing or motion graphics; (7) Experience with tools like Canva or Power Point for template design; (8) Prior experience in think tanks, research organisations, publishing, or media preferred.
5. COMPENSATION OFFERED: The gross compensation budgeted for the position is INR 75,000/- per month. The offer made to the selected candidate shall be commensurate with qualifications, experience, and salary history.

title: Senior Programme Manager – Nutrition
department: Grant Writing, Management and Administration, Program Leadership
jobDescription:
1. POSITION VACANT: Senior Programme Manager
- Nutrition, Large Philanthropic Organisation, Mumbai
2. ORGANISATIONAL BACKGROUND: Our client is a respected philanthropic organisation with a vision of advancing humanitarian values and nation-building. The organisation drives social and economic development across India by focusing on health, education, livelihoods, water and sanitation, social inclusion, environment, and disaster response. Our client's mission is to empower underserved communities through innovative programmes and strategic collaborations with governments, civil society, and global partners, creating sustainable impact aligned with national priorities and the UN Sustainable Development Goals.
3. JOB DESCRIPTION/

RESPONSIBILITIES:
Reporting to the Head
- Nutrition , the Senior Programme Manager
- Nutrition (SPMN) shall lead the design, expansion, and management of the organisation's nutrition initiatives across India. The role combines strategic vision with technical expertise, ensuring programmes are evidence-based, scalable, and impactful. Acting as both strategist and implementer, the incumbent shall drive partnerships, oversee grants, and generate knowledge products that influence practice and policy. With a focus on improving nutrition outcomes for vulnerable communities, this role demands strong leadership, cross-sectoral collaboration, and the ability to translate research and innovation into sustainable programmes. The role requires a senior nutrition professional who can operate at portfolio level, contribute to programme strategy and design, and engage credibly with senior internal and external stakeholders, while also ensuring disciplined programme and grant management. The incumbent must understand the organisation's role as a philanthropy and grant-making institution, and be able to support, guide, co-design, evaluate and fund partner-led interventions, rather than approach the role as a direct implementation position. Key

RESPONSIBILITIES:
(A) Strategy: (1) Contribute towards reviewing and updating strategy from time to time in consultation with the Theme Head, Senior Advisor and Head of Programme. This will necessitate landscaping and situation analysis, need-gap assessment of nutrition, health and inter-related domains by conducting background desk research and real-life ground assessments and identifying potential needs; (2) Contribute to the expansion of the organisation's nutrition programme with a focus on high-priority geographies; (3) Contribute to strategising internal collaborations with other themes such as health or education within the organisation; (4) Develop comprehensive programme plans, delivery models, monitoring frameworks and scale-up roadmaps for new and existing nutrition initiatives and programmes; (5) Identify and initiate strategic nutrition partnerships with like-minded stakeholders; (6) Initiate, support and deliver on any high-priority assignments as mandated by the organisation. (7) Contribute analytically and strategically to programme direction, rather than only support implementation of approved interventions. (B) Technical: (1) Review latest and best practices in nutrition and offer thought leadership on nutrition-specific and nutrition-sensitive programme and research development as per the organisation's vision and strategy. The candidate shall formulate problem statements from time to time; (2) Adopt best practices and apply these in programme design and management, and promote cross-sectoral linkages, cross-theme linkages and integration of cross-cutting issues; (3) Build a pipeline of proposals for developing the nutrition portfolio in alignment with thematic strategy and multi-year grant-making goals. Co-create concepts and proposals for shaping initiatives with potential partners. Develop and float RFPs and work in evaluations of submitted proposals; (4) Undertake comprehensive evaluation of relevant concepts and proposals for grant-making at regular intervals. Engage and involve external experts in the evaluation process as per the organisation's norms; (5) Assess proposals not only for technical merit, but also for operational feasibility, ground readiness, financial logic, cost-effectiveness and likely results; (6) Lead and organise sectoral meetings, roundtables, consultations, and workshops as per plan; (7) Develop and execute monitoring, learning and evaluation frameworks to develop innovative and/or tested theories of change for effective and feasible models. (C) Programme Management: (1) Independently manage different complex programmes and initiatives. This shall include end-to-end responsibility from onboarding grants, management and closure, adhering to processes, monitoring and supervision of grants/programmes, and offering support to grantees. Ensure timely reports and fund disbursals; This includes critical monitoring that goes beyond routine field visits and reports, with timely identification of red/yellow flags and basic programme-finance signals such as utilisation, cash-flow or budget patterns, in collaboration with finance colleagues; (2) Identify learnings and lessons from projects and initiatives and develop knowledge products; (3) Work in collaboration with other themes and cross-functional units such as strategy, grant management, finance, legal, partnership and communications, as and when required and assigned; (4) Create high-quality content for mixed audiences, such as case studies, reports, concept notes, pitch decks, articles/ blog posts, etc.; (5) Develop annual work plans and budgets collaboratively; (6) Manage relationships with respective grantees and partners; (7) Liaise and serve as a key point of contact with stakeholders including government and other partners. (D) Key Stakeholders: (1) Relationship within the organisation: Theme Heads, Function Heads and departmental teams; (2) Relationship outside the organisation: Government officials and applicant organisations.
4. QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE AND COMPETENCIES: Qualifications Applicants must have a Ph D, Master's or PG Diploma in Public Health Nutrition, Global Health, Public Health, Food and Nutrition Policies and Programmes, Public Policy, Development Studies and related disciplines; or an MD in Community Health with interest in nutrition. Experience (1) About 10-15 years of experience in public health nutrition, nutritional biology, food and related programme development, research and policy; (2) Candidates should be able to demonstrate experience in shaping or strengthening programme strategy, designing scalable interventions, developing theories of change/results frameworks, and translating evidence into programme decisions; (3) Prior experience in philanthropy and grant-making will be an asset; (4) Experience in research and programme evaluation will be essential; (5) Experience in landscaping and gap analysis, curating problem statements, theory of change, logical framework analysis or results framework is strongly desirable; (6) Selected experience in food systems, supply chain, logistics and solutioning around gaps and needs related to the triple burden of malnutrition, including undernutrition, micronutrient deficiencies and overweight/ overnutrition, will be an advantage; (7) Programme and grant management exposure and past experience in budget management is important; (8) Experience in partnerships and relationship management with diverse stakeholders; (9) Experience in analytical writing, including proposal notes, publications, technical papers, and presentations, as well as external representation, will be an added advantage. Skills and Competencies (1) Problem solving, particularly in public health and nutrition; (2) Data and innovation orientation; (3) Strategic thinking and planning; (4) Ability to move comfortably between field realities, evidence, programme architecture and leadership-level decision-making; (5) Agility and adaptability to organisation-level changes; including comfort with evolving institutional strategies and ways of working; (6) Planning, organising, leading and supervising; with the maturity to function as a dependable second line of leadership when required; (7) High integrity, ethical, responsible and accountable; (8) Deep commitment, passion and experience in the social development sector, along with domain knowledge in nutrition. Public health competence is valuable; (9) Good understanding and experience of using theory of change-based programme design; (10) Skilled in proposal assessment and evaluation; (11) Excellent communication skills with command over spoken and written English and Hindi; including the ability to prepare cogent evidence-based notes and present/defend recommendations before senior internal and external stakeholders; (12) Knowledge of field realities and social complexities with a focus on communities is essential; (13) Proactive, self-starter, who can work independently and collaboratively; with a go-getter orientation and the ability to reach out to internal colleagues, external experts and sector peers when shaping or evaluating ideas; (14) Team player and collaborative with good interpersonal skills; (15) Proficient in computer skills, including Outlook, Word, Excel, Power Point, SPSS, Google Suite, etc.; (16) Respect and practice diversity, equity and inclusion.
5. COMPENSATION OFFERED: The compensation offered for the position is competitive and commensurate with experience and salary history.
6. LOCATION & NATURE OF APPOINTMENT: (1) Location: Mumbai (mandatory travel to different locations in the country, including remote areas, at least 10-15 days in a month); (2) Nature of Appointment: Fixed-term employment for three years.

title: Senior Research Leader – Climate & Sustainability
department: Climate Research, Project Management, Strategic Partnerships
jobDescription:
1. POSITION VACANT: Senior Research Leader
- Climate & Sustainability, Leading Think Tank, New Delhi
2. ORGANISATION BACKGROUND: Founded and headquartered in India, the organisation is a highly respected research and policy organisation working at the intersection of sustainability, climate change, environment, energy, and development. It undertakes evidence-based research, policy engagement, advisory work, and multi-stakeholder collaborations with national and international partners. The organisation has a long-standing reputation for knowledge leadership and for shaping practical solutions to complex sustainability challenges.
3. JOB DESCRIPTION/

RESPONSIBILITIES:
The Senior Research Leader
- Climate & Sustainability will provide strategic leadership to research, advisory, knowledge, and policy-facing initiatives in the areas of climate change, sustainability, environmental management, resilience, and sustainable development. The position requires a seasoned professional who combines strong domain credibility with the ability to shape research agendas, build and manage funded portfolios, cultivate strategic partnerships, guide multidisciplinary teams, and translate evidence into policy, practice, and organisational influence. The role is suited to a strategic professional who is comfortable working across research, policy, programme leadership, proposal development, donor and partner engagement, and organisational representation. Key

RESPONSIBILITIES:
(A) Research & Knowledge Initiatives: (1) Provide strategic direction to research, advisory, and knowledge initiatives in the areas of climate change, sustainability, environmental management, resilience, and sustainable development; (2) Lead the conceptualisation, design, and delivery of high-quality research, analytical studies, policy briefs, technical reports, and knowledge products addressing emerging environmental and sustainability challenges; (3) Develop innovative and evidence-based approaches to issues such as climate adaptation and mitigation, environmental sustainability, natural resource management, resilience, circular economy, air quality, energy transitions, and related development priorities; (4) Contribute to publications, thought leadership, and policy-facing outputs that strengthen the organisation's credibility and influence in the climate and sustainability domain; (5) Represent the organisation in national and international forums, expert groups, conferences, and knowledge platforms. (B) Fundraising and Strategic Partnerships: (1) Lead resource mobilization efforts to secure grants, donor funding, and strategic investments for the organisation's work in climate, sustainability, environment, and resilience; (2) Develop competitive concept notes, proposals, grant applications, and consulting bids to expand the organisation's funding pipeline and revenue base; (3) Build and manage strategic relationships with donors, foundations, government agencies, multilateral organisations, industry partners, and other funding stakeholders; (4) Identify and pursue emerging funding opportunities and partnership avenues aligned with climate action, sustainable development, and environmental priorities. (C) Program Oversight & Delivery: (1) Provide strategic oversight to a portfolio of climate, sustainability, environment, and development programmes, ensuring quality, relevance, and impact; (2) Guide multidisciplinary teams comprising researchers, technical specialists, policy experts, and programme professionals; (3) Ensure effective planning, implementation, monitoring, learning, reporting, and dissemination of outcomes and research findings. (D) Organizational Strategy & Growth: (1) Contribute to organizational strategy and long-term positioning in climate change, sustainability, environment, and development policy domains; (2) Track emerging policy, regulatory, technological, and research developments relevant to climate action and sustainable development; (3) Represent the organisation in policy dialogues, advisory committees, stakeholder consultations, and strategic engagements with government, development partners, academia, and industry.
4. QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE AND COMPETENCIES:

QUALIFICATIONS:
Advanced degree (Master's or Ph.D.) in Climate Change, Environmental Science, Sustainability, or a related discipline from a reputed institution. Experience: (1) Minimum 15 years of experience in climate change, sustainability, environmental science, or related fields, including leading research programs, managing complex and multidisciplinary research projects, developing funded research portfolios, and delivering high-quality research and knowledge outputs; (2) Experience securing and managing research funding through grants, donor-supported programs, strategic partnerships, and collaborative research initiatives; (3) Experience in building and managing multidisciplinary teams, research networks, and partnerships across government, academia, development organizations, philanthropic foundations, and the private sector; (4) Track record of shaping research agendas, influencing policy and practice, and advancing the visibility, credibility, and impact of research and knowledge initiatives. Skills and Competencies: (1) Advanced subject matter expertise and thought leadership across climate change, sustainability, environmental management, and resilience frameworks; (2) Experience securing and managing research funding through grants, strategic partnerships, and collaborative programs; (3) Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship-management skills, with credibility to engage senior stakeholders across government, donors, development partners, academia, philanthropy, and industry; (4) Leadership experience managing multidisciplinary teams, complex programs, and high-impact initiatives; (5) Excellent communication, representation, and influencing skills, with the ability to translate evidence into policy, practice, and organisational positioning.
5. COMPENSATION OFFERED: Gross compensation budgeted for the position is attractive and in alignment with salaries paid by leading I/NGOs for leadership roles. The offer made to the selected candidate shall be commensurate with qualifications, experience, and salary history.
